overview.headline: Drag force depends on density speed shape and reference area choice

keyPoints.point: Drag depends on air density and velocity squared and body shape
keyPoints.quote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity, the air’s viscosity and compressibility

keyPoints.point: Drag coefficient variable collects complex drag effects into single equation value
keyPoints.quote: For drag, this variable is called the drag coefficient, designated “Cd.”

keyPoints.point: Drag coefficients are determined experimentally using wind tunnel measurements
keyPoints.quote: Drag coefficients are almost always determined experimentally using a wind tunnel.

keyPoints.point: Reference area choice affects coefficient value while total drag remains consistent
keyPoints.quote: Notice that the area (A) given in the drag equation is given as a reference area.

keyPoints.point: Dynamic pressure combines density and velocity squared divided by half factor
keyPoints.quote: The combination of terms “density times the square of the velocity divided by two” is called the dynamic pressure

keyTerms.gloss: Resistance force depending on density and velocity
keyTerms.quote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity

keyTerms.gloss: Single variable collecting complex drag dependence for calculation
keyTerms.quote: For drag, this variable is called the drag coefficient, designated “Cd.”

keyTerms.gloss: Chosen area basis used in drag equation calculations
keyTerms.quote: Notice that the area (A) given in the drag equation is given as a reference area.

keyTerms.gloss: Air mass per volume designated by letter rho
keyTerms.quote: In the equation given above, the density is designated by the letter rho (ρ).

keyTerms.gloss: Combined density and velocity effect appearing in pressure equation
keyTerms.quote: The combination of terms “density times the square of the velocity divided by two” is called the dynamic pressure
